actor: Auth key lifecycle product manager, Tailscale identity and device enrollment
job: Deciding what a newly minted auth key does out of the box, after the postmortem named long-lived reusable keys as the gap.
outcome: A default node-enrollment ceiling on newly minted keys, applying on a fresh tailnet with no customer configuration.
motivation: Documentation and prompts leave the default alone; only the issuer can bound how many nodes one key enrolls.

task.who: Tailscale auth key product management with control plane engineering
task.what: Specify a default enrollment ceiling for newly minted auth keys
task.where: Tailscale auth key lifecycle product specification and roadmap
task.why: Reusability is stamped at mint time and cannot be revoked downstream
task.how: Reusable keys carry a default node ceiling unless raised

actor: Post-incident engineering review lead, Tailscale security
job: Converting the recovered intrusion timeline of 136 stolen keys, 181 enrolled nodes and roughly four and a half days into blast-radius requirements.
outcome: A written finding that reusability, not credential scope, produced the node count, aimed at the key issuing default.
motivation: No product flaw was found, so the only lever left is what the product ships enabled by default.

task.who: Tailscale security engineering and incident review staff
task.what: Trace the node count back to key reusability at mint
task.where: Tailscale internal incident review and customer tailnet audit logs
task.why: Ceiling design needs the axis that actually produced 181 nodes
task.how: Recovered enrollment records and node registration timestamps from the tailnet

actor: Continuous integration platform engineer, large enterprise tailnet operator
job: Moving headless build fleet enrollment off long-lived reusable keys onto ephemeral, federated credentials issued per job.
outcome: A build fleet that keeps working when reusable keys stop being unbounded, removing the objection to changing the default.
motivation: Reusable keys exist because build fleets create nodes with nobody present; the default holds until that job is covered.

task.who: Platform engineering and build infrastructure teams at tailnet customers
task.what: Re-issue build node credentials per job instead of one reusable key
task.where: Enterprise continuous integration pipelines and node provisioning scripts
task.why: The vendor keeps the default until the unattended fleet job survives
task.how: Workload identity federation or a credential-injecting proxy per build

actor: Workload identity federation specification editor, machine identity standards group
job: Finishing the profile that lets an unattended machine present a short-lived, verifiable identity instead of carrying a reusable secret.
outcome: A federated enrollment path mature enough that a network vendor can bound reusable keys without stranding headless fleets.
motivation: Bounding the old credential is only safe once the replacement is interoperable across issuers and cloud runtimes.

task.who: Specification editors and implementers in the machine identity group
task.what: Publish an interoperable federated enrollment profile for unattended nodes
task.where: Open machine identity specification drafts and reference implementations
task.why: Named as the control that belonged where the reusable key sat
task.how: Attestation-backed short-lived credentials with cross-issuer conformance tests

actor: Control plane registration engineer, Tailscale coordination server
job: Building a per-key enrollment counter so the coordination server can refuse a registration once a key passes its node limit.
outcome: Server-side enforcement that makes a bounded default meaningful rather than advisory, counted at the registration endpoint.
motivation: A default nobody enforces is a prompt; the count has to be held where nodes actually join.

task.who: Tailscale control plane and node registration engineering
task.what: Add per-key enrollment counters and refusal at node registration
task.where: Tailscale coordination server registration path and key records
task.why: A bound only holds where enrollment is actually counted
task.how: Durable per-key counters plus registration rejection and audit events

actor: New tailnet onboarding defaults owner, Tailscale account provisioning
job: Setting what a freshly created tailnet ships with, given the intrusion ran on a configuration nobody had touched.
outcome: A fresh tailnet where the enrollment bound applies before any administrator opens a settings page.
motivation: The claim is about untouched defaults, so a bound gated behind an opt-in switch does not count.

task.who: Tailscale onboarding, provisioning and default policy owners
task.what: Move the enrollment bound into fresh tailnet provisioning defaults
task.where: Tailscale tailnet creation flow and initial policy template
task.why: A bound behind an opt-in switch is configuration, not default
task.how: Default policy template applied at tailnet creation, no toggle

actor: Multiplayer agent harness maintainer, open-source per-room scope projects
job: Shipping per-person and per-room keychain views, and stating in the credential docs what scoping cannot do about reuse.
outcome: An integration requirement, read across thousands of forks, that credential issuers hand harnesses single-use or bounded keys.
motivation: A per-person keychain holding one reusable key carries the same blast radius, delivered more tidily.

task.who: Open-source harness maintainers and security posture contributors
task.what: State that harness scoping cannot revoke reuse granted at mint
task.where: Harness credential handling documentation and keychain integration guides
task.why: Downstream scoping cannot take back reusability, so demand moves upstream
task.how: Keychain integration guides requesting single-use credentials from issuers

actor: Product documentation lead, Tailscale developer docs and changelog
job: Writing the auth key reference and changelog entry that states the shipped enrollment ceiling as behaviour, not as advice.
outcome: Published Tailscale material describing the bound a new key carries by default, the artifact that settles the claim.
motivation: A behaviour nobody documents is invisible to customers; the reference page is where a default becomes a commitment.

task.who: Tailscale documentation and developer relations writers
task.what: Document the shipped enrollment ceiling in the auth key reference
task.where: Tailscale product documentation, changelog and engineering blog
task.why: Documented shipped behaviour outranks a best-practice recommendation page
task.how: Reference page and changelog entry describing default key behaviour
